quick.summary: Why every tester passed and the feature still failed, and how to word a test task.
quick.takeaway: Give the goal and the situation. Never the button.

beats.line: All five testers found the export button. After launch, nobody can. What happened?
Click export to download your report.
You told them the word on the button. That is an instruction.
A task gives a goal and a situation, in their words.
What if they get stuck and can’t finish?
Then you found the problem. That is why you test.
Your manager wants last month’s figures by email. Show me what you would do.
Now you see whether they can find it alone.

quiz.question: Which is the best task for a usability test of an export feature?
options: Your manager wants last month’s figures by email. Show me what you would do.
Click export to download your report.
Find the export button in the top menu.
quiz.explanation: It gives a realistic goal without naming the control, so you learn whether people can find it.

quiz.question: A usability test task should name the button you want people to use.
quiz.explanation: Naming the button gives the answer away. A task describes the goal and lets people find the way.
